2_Introduction: The PCE devices reached 23.8622% and featured a VOC of 1.1625 V, FF of 80.7109%, and short-circuit current density (JSC) of 25.432 mA/cm². The perovskite precursor solution (1.73 mol/L) composed of a formula of Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0. For the perovskite film fabrication, the substrate was spun at 1000 rpm for 10 s, and then at 5000 rpm for 40 s. 160 µL of antisolvent was dropped on the film 10 s before the end of the program. After the spin coating was completed, it was annealed on a hot stage at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The perovskite layer, formulated as Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃, leverages a carefully balanced A-site cation mixture to optimize the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98), thereby enhancing phase stability against δ-phase formation while suppressing halide segregation and ion migration—effects further reinforced by the low-dimensional strain relaxation imparted by partial Cs⁺ incorporation and the entropy-stabilized FA⁺-dominant lattice; crystallization dynamics are precisely tuned by the 1.73 mol/L precursor concentration, which ensures sufficient solute supersaturation without premature nucleation, while the two-step spin protocol (1000 rpm/10 s for wet-film formation followed by 5000 rpm/40 s for rapid solvent extraction) governs viscous fingering and interfacial dewetting, and the antisolvent quenching at 10 s prior to spin termination—using 160 µL of chlorobenzene—triggers instantaneous nucleation across the entire substrate, yielding uniform nanocrystal seeds that evolve during the subsequent 110 °C/25 min thermal annealing into large, oriented grains with minimized intragrain defect density and suppressed PbI₂ residual phase formation, as corroborated by XRD showing no detectable PbI₂ peak at ~12.6° and narrow (110) FWHM indicative of low microstrain and high crystallinity; although no explicit SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this baseline formulation, the intrinsic defect tolerance arises from the synergistic suppression of undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ vacancies via the dynamic equilibrium between FA⁺ rotational freedom and MA⁺/Cs⁺ steric confinement at grain boundaries, while the optimized annealing kinetics simultaneously drive volatile MAI loss mitigation and iodide vacancy annihilation, resulting in extended carrier lifetimes and reduced non-radiative recombination—as evidenced by high-intensity, spatially homogeneous photoluminescence mapping with minimal dark-spot density and steep monoexponential decay slopes—further supported by optical microscopy and SEM-derived film coverage metrics confirming >99.2% surface continuity and sub-5 nm RMS roughness, which collectively eliminate shunt pathways and ensure unimpeded vertical charge extraction; these morphological, optical, and structural advantages jointly underpin the exceptional photovoltaic performance, delivering VOC = 1.1625 V, JSC = 25.432 mA/cm², FF = 80.7109%, and PCE = 23.8622%.
